events.title: Proposed ruling: refund_full $6.61 (model confidence 0.94)
events.body:
The fee in dispute is a rider-cancellation charge: cancelled_by = rider [F2], so the fee can only enter through NS-0's rider branch, which sends an on-demand booking to NS-4. NS-4 charges nothing where the rider cancels within 3 minutes of matching (≤ 3:00) and charges $6.61 only where the cancellation comes later. The timeline records acceptance at 18:23:00 and rider cancellation at 18:25:30, i.e. 2 min 30 s (150 s), and the fare record shows $6.61 actually charged [F2][F5]. On those settled values the charge fails its own precondition, so the whole $6.61 disputed item is refundable: refund_full of $6.61 [F5][F2][NS-0][NS-4].

The alternative basis for retaining the fee — a driver-side no-show — is also unavailable, though it is not needed. No arrival was ever recorded: driver_arrived_at is null and driver_pressed_here_at is null, so NS-1 (i) is not met, and the GPS record shows the driver's closest approach was 1816 m at 18:25:30 and that he never came within 200 m of the pickup, so NS-1 (ii) and (iii) cannot be satisfied either [F1][F3][F4][NS-1]. With none of NS-1's conditions met, the fee cannot stand on that branch and NS-2's refund outcome follows [F3][F4][F1][NS-2].

The driver's written statement that he "was on his way when the rider cancelled" is consistent with the system records (no arrival ever recorded) and is not in genuine conflict with them, so nothing turns on the record-vs-statement priority here; it in any event cannot supply the NS-1 preconditions — a statement of being en route is not an arrival confirmation, and being en route is exactly what the records already show [F10][F1][F3][F4][NS-1]. His 18:24 chat message ("5 min more, traffic is slow") likewise describes a car still on the way, which the rider read and acted on [F8][F7].

Ryde's published rule gives no free-cancellation right merely because the driver is late or not yet arrived, and NS-4 says so expressly: lateness is not the rider's free-cancellation ground, and the rider's remedy for that is the NS-7 manual route [F1][F8][NS-4][NS-7]. Here the rider does not need it — the 3-minute rule alone decides the case, so the outcome does not depend on the driver's position.

No account flag arises. RD-6 requires an established case against the driver plus a prior upheld route dispute within 90 days; the driver's profile shows 0 disputes and 0 upheld (and the rider's the same), and the NS-2 add-on for tapping "I'm Here" while away from the pickup is not triggered because the driver never tapped at all [F15][F14][F4][RD-6][NS-2]. claims.assertion: The driver was never at the pickup point: his closest approach to Jurong East MRT was 1816 m, and the GPS record states he never came within 200 m at any time before the cancellation.
No arrival was ever recorded — driver_pressed_here_at is null and driver_arrived_at is null, so requirement (i) of NS-1 (driver pressed "I'm Here" or platform auto-arrival) is not met.

In any event, since the driver was 1816 m away when the rider cancelled, he cannot have waited more than 3 continuous minutes within 200 m of the pickup point, so requirement (iii) of NS-1 fails as well.

The driver's own messages confirm he was still en route and not at the pickup point: at 18:24 he wrote "5 min more, traffic is slow", i.e. he expected to arrive about 18:29, after the rider's 18:25:30 cancellation.
Because NS-1 (i), (ii) and (iii) all fail, the $6.61 cancellation fee on the rider's record is not payable and must be refunded in full.

The rider cancelled 2 min 30 s after acceptance, within the 3-minute window; although NS-4's free-cancellation window is not itself needed here, the timing shows the rider acted promptly once it was clear the driver was not near.
No safety ground appears in the chat or statements — the driver's written statement is merely "I was on my way when the rider cancelled" — so no SAFE-1/SAFE-2 escalation is warranted on this record.
The driver has 1043 trips in 90 days and a clean dispute record, so the rider does not seek any account flag; the requested relief is limited to the $6.61 fee.

weaknesses: The rider did cancel rather than wait, and the driver was apologetic in chat (F8, F10); the driver may argue the rider should have waited the extra 5 minutes rather than cancel — but NS-4 gives no free-cancellation right on late arrival, and his lateness is not a defence to charging a fee whose statutory preconditions (F3, F4) were never met.

The driver's statement (F10) claims he was on his way; it conflicts with the GPS record that he never came within 200 m (F1), and system records win over statements, but the judge may still weigh the statement.

The cancellation fee amount comes only from the fare record (F5) and the timeline (F2); if the judge treats the NS-1 preconditions as unproven rather than disproven, the case could be sent to manual review (G12) instead of an automatic refund.

The driver's written statement that he "was on his way" is not disputed by any system record — no arrival was ever recorded at the pickup point — but it also does not support retaining the fee, since the branch that would justify it (NS-1) is unmet on the timeline facts.

The chat shows the rider asking for the ETA and the driver replying "5 min more, traffic is slow", so the rider knew the car was still several minutes away; that is relevant to the rider's expectation but, since Ryde publishes no driver-late free-cancellation rule, it does not itself decide the fee — the 3-minute rule does.
